description.narrative:
The Youth Nexus Innovation Labs will empower young people in Bo and Kailahun to design and test low-cost environmental solutions using portable E-STEM “innovation-in-a-bag” toolkits. Through these kits, youth will collect real water and soil data, co-create ideaswith communities, and build simple prototypes that improve water safety, soil health, and agroforestry practices. Fifty marginalized youth (18–35) will lead the full innovation cycle—from diagnostics to prototyping, testing, and sharing results with district stakeholders. The project will generate practical evidence, locally adapted solutions, and Youth Resilience Briefs that communities and institutions can continue using beyond the grant, helping establish a sustainable youth-led innovation system in Sierra Leone.
The project aims to empower youth to design and test low-cost solutions for water and agroforestry challenges in Bo and Kailahun. Objectives include training 50 youth, running 3–4 innovation cycles, and producing evidence and prototypes. Key activities are operating mobile E-STEM lab -in- bag packs,community diagnostics, co-design sessions, prototype testing, and sharing findings through Youth Resilience Briefs and district presentations.

participating-org.narrative:
We envision a future where sustainable development, social equity, and environmental resilience converge, fostering a thriving society through collective action and innovative solutions.
Mission: We are dedicated to fostering holistic well-being communities through a mission that integrates environmental sustainability, community health, sports, education, entrepreneurship, mental health, peace <(><<)>(><(>&<)><(><<)>)> cohesion, and gender and disability rights.
Action for Community Resilience Group (ACRG) is a non-profit organization in Sierra Leone that fosters community resilience and sustainable development. Our mission is to empower local communities through various initiatives, focusing on education, health, and social well-being. With a commitment to positive change, we work collaboratively to build resilient communities that thrive in the face of challenges. Join us in creating a brighter and more resilient future for Sierra Leone.
The Action for Community Resilience Group (ACRG) is governed by a 7-member Board that includes anindependent Chair, community stakeholders, a youth representative, and key governance roles such as the President and Compliance Officer. The Board provides strategic direction and oversight while ensuring community perspectives guide decisions. Day-to-day operations are led entirely by young professionals aged 18–35, who manage planning, field work, partnerships, and reporting. Continuous feedback between the Board, youth staff, and communities keeps ACRG transparent, accountable, and grounded in real local needs.
